title: The Tale of the Second Lady, the Flogged One

paragraphs.en: After my father's death, I inherited a substantial sum of money. Shortly after, I married the wealthiest man in Baghdad, and we lived happily for a year. Following his passing, I received ninety thousand dinars as part of my inheritance.
paragraphs.zh: 在我父亲去世后，我继承了一笔不小的财富。不久之后，我在巴格达嫁给了最富有的人之一，我们幸福地生活了一年。在他去世后，我又收到了九万迪纳尔的遗产。

paragraphs.en: My life was prosperous; I bought gold jewelry, clothes, and embroideries worth ten thousand dinars each, and my reputation grew in the city.
paragraphs.zh: 我的生活颇为富裕，我买了价值一万第纳尔的金饰、衣物和刺绣，名声也在城中逐渐响亮起来。

paragraphs.en: One day, an old woman visited me. She was visibly aged, with pale, scabby skin, a bent body, matted gray hair, and broken teeth. Her eyes were hollow and bleary, and she had a runny nose.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，一位老妇人来访。她明显苍老，皮肤苍白而布满疮疤，身体佝偻，灰白的头发杂乱无章，牙齿残缺不全。她的双眼凹陷且模糊不清，鼻孔还流着清涕。

paragraphs.en: The poet described her as having seven defects on her face, the least of which was due to fate.
paragraphs.zh: 诗人形容她脸上有七处缺陷，其中最小的也是命中注定的。

paragraphs.en: The old woman greeted me, kissing the ground before me. She said, "My lady, I have an orphaned daughter whose unveiling and wedding night are tonight. We are strangers in this city and do not know anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人向我行礼，跪在地上亲吻道：“夫人，我有个孤儿女儿，今晚要举行她的成年礼和婚礼。我们是这个城市的陌生人，不认识任何人。

paragraphs.en: If you come to her wedding, you will earn a reward in Heaven. The ladies of this city will hear about your visit and follow suit, honoring us with your presence and making my daughter happy."
paragraphs.zh: 如果你参加她的婚礼，你将在天堂得到奖赏。这个城市里的女人们会听说你来了，也会效仿，让你的光临增添我们的荣耀，也让我的女儿高兴。”

paragraphs.en: The old woman then recited these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人随后念诵了这几行诗句：

paragraphs.en: We own that your visit is an honor That cannot be performed by another.
paragraphs.zh: 我们荣幸之至，您的来访实属难得，绝无他人可替代。

paragraphs.en: She wept until I relented and agreed. "I will do it for God," I said, "and your bridegroom shall not see you unveiled except in my clothes." Overjoyed, she kissed my feet.
paragraphs.zh: 她哭得我心软，最终答应了。我说：“我会为你做的，为了上帝，你的新郎除了在我穿的衣服下见不到你。”她喜出望外，亲吻了我的脚。

paragraphs.en: At suppertime, she returned with a smile, informing me that most of the city's ladies were already gathered. I dressed and followed her and my maids to an alleyway where we approached a door adorned with a black curtain and a golden lamp.
paragraphs.zh: 晚饭时间，她带着微笑回来了，告诉我城里大多数女眷已经聚集在一起了。我赶紧换好衣服，跟着她和侍女来到一条小巷，在那里我们靠近了一扇挂着黑色帷幕、点缀着金色灯盏的门。

paragraphs.en: Inside, silk carpets covered the floor, and lighted candles formed an avenue leading to a couch encrusted with gems. Suddenly, a girl emerged from behind the curtain, radiant like the half moon. Her face was as beautiful as the full moon or rising sun.
paragraphs.zh: 室内铺设着丝绸地毯，点燃的蜡烛排列成一条通向镶嵌宝石的长沙发的小径。突然，一个女孩从帘幕后走出，光彩照人，犹如新月一般。她的脸庞美丽得如同满月或初升的太阳。

paragraphs.en: She descended from the couch and greeted me, "Welcome, dear sister." Then she recited:
paragraphs.zh: 她从榻上起身，微笑着迎接我：“亲爱的姐姐，欢迎你。”随后她吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: If the house could know who has visited, It would rejoice and kiss the very dust.
paragraphs.zh: 如果这座房子能知道谁来过，它一定会欢欣鼓舞，甚至吻扫地的尘土。

paragraphs.en: The Second Lady approached me, saying her brother desired to marry me. I agreed, and she introduced a young man who was handsome and graceful. He charmed me with his sweet coquettishness and enchanting eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 第二女郎走近我，说她的兄弟有意娶我为妻。我应允了，她介绍了一个英俊温雅的年轻人。他以甜美的挑逗和迷人的目光赢得了我的好感。

paragraphs.en: We spent a delightful night together.
paragraphs.zh: 我们共度了一个愉快的夜晚。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, he slaughtered sheep in gratitude and treated me kindly. For a month, we lived happily together.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天一早，他宰了一只羊表示感谢，并对我十分体贴。我们在一起度过了一个月的快乐时光。

paragraphs.en: One day, I asked permission to go to the market to buy fabric. My companion led me to a young merchant with excellent goods. Entering his shop, I saw him—a slender, handsome youth, much like the poet's description:
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，我请求同行的人带我去市场买布料。她领我来到了一位年轻商人的店铺，那里货物甚好。踏入他的店铺，我见到了他——一个身材修长、相貌俊朗的青年，与诗人笔下的描述颇为相似：

paragraphs.en: Here is a slender youth whose hair and face
paragraphs.zh: 这里是一位身材瘦削的少年，他的头发和面容

paragraphs.en: were fair as morning dew.
paragraphs.zh: 如同晨露般清新美丽。

paragraphs.en: The old lady instructed the man to show them some fabric. He displayed several pieces, a few of which I liked. When asked for the price, he demanded a kiss instead.
paragraphs.zh: 老妇人让那男子拿出一些布料给他们看。他拿出了几块，其中有几块我挺喜欢的。当问到价格时，他竟索要了一个吻作为回报。

paragraphs.en: Tempted by the old woman's suggestion, I turned my face towards him. He bit off a piece of flesh from my cheek and fled with his goods. The old woman, weeping over my injury, urged me to feign illness at home.
paragraphs.zh: 受那位老妇人建议的诱惑，我转头望向他。只见他咬下我脸颊一块肉，带着战利品逃之夭夭。老妇人在为我的伤痛哭泣，催促我在家中装病。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard that the flogged girl spoke to the Commander of the Faithful. The old lady comforted her, assuring her that God had spared her worse. She advised us to leave before the incident became public knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说那个受鞭笞的女孩曾与至高长官交谈。老妇人安慰她说，上帝已经保佑她免遭更糟的命运。她劝我们赶紧离开，以免此事闹得满城风雨。

paragraphs.en: At home, I pretended to be ill and covered myself up. The old woman brought me remedies to heal my cheek within three days.
paragraphs.zh: 在家裡，我裝作生病了，把自己裹得嚴严实实的。老婦人帶來了一些藥膏，說三天內就能治好我的臉頰。

paragraphs.en: In the evening, my husband entered and asked, "What is troubling you?" I replied, "I have a headache." He lit a candle and examined my face.
paragraphs.zh: 傍晚时分，丈夫走了进来，问道：“你这是怎么了？”我回答说：“我头疼。”他点燃蜡烛，仔细看了看我的脸。

paragraphs.en: Seeing the wound on my cheek, he inquired, "How did this happen?"
paragraphs.zh: 看到我脸颊上的伤痕，他问道：“这是怎么弄的？”

paragraphs.en: I explained, "While buying fabric at the market today, a camel driver with firewood jostled me in a narrow passage, tearing my veil and cutting my cheek."
paragraphs.zh: 我解释道：“今天在市场上买布时，一个挑柴的驼夫在狭窄的小巷里挤了我一下，扯破了我的面纱，还划伤了我的脸颊。”

paragraphs.en: He declared, "Tomorrow I will ask the city governor to hang every camel driver." I interjected, "My lord, innocent men should not be punished for this."
paragraphs.zh: 他脱口而出：“明天我将要求城主把所有的骆驼夫都处以绞刑。”我插嘴道：“我的 Lord，无辜的人不应为此受罚。”

paragraphs.en: He pressed further, asking who was responsible. I responded, "I was riding a rented donkey when it stumbled due to the driver's harshness, throwing me onto glass and cutting my cheek."
paragraphs.zh: 他追问是谁的责任。我答道：“那天我骑着一匹租来的驴子，因为赶路人鞭打得太狠，驴子受惊乱了蹄子，结果摔到了玻璃上，划破了我的脸颊。”

paragraphs.en: He vowed, "Tomorrow, I will go to Ja’far the Barmakid and demand that every donkey driver and sweeper be punished." I pleaded, "My lord, do not punish others for this."
paragraphs.zh: 他发誓道：“明天，我要去找巴尔马克的贾法尔，要求严惩每一个赶驴的和打扫卫生的人。”我哀求道：“我的主上，请不要因为这件事惩罚别人。”

paragraphs.en: He continued to press until I reluctantly admitted, "I suffered what God had destined for me." Enraged, he cried out. Three black slaves entered, dragging me from my bed and placing me on the floor.
paragraphs.zh: 他继续施压，直到我不情愿地承认：“我承受了上帝为我准备的苦难。”他气得大喊起来。三个黑奴进来，把我从床上拖起，放在地上。

paragraphs.en: He ordered one slave to sit on my knees, another to hold my head, and a third to draw his sword. He commanded, "Sa’d, strike her with one blow and cut her in half, each of you carrying one half to throw into the Tigris for the fish."
paragraphs.zh: 他命令一个奴隶坐在我膝上，另一个托住我的头，第三个则拔出剑来。他喝道：“萨德，每人一击，把她劈成两半，你们各自拖一半扔进底格里斯河喂鱼。”

paragraphs.en: Angered, he recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他气愤之下脱口而出：“怒火中烧，我吟诵道：”

paragraphs.en: "If there be one who shares the one I love, I'll kill my love even though my soul dies, Saying, 'Better nobly to die, O soul, Than share a love for which another vies.'"
paragraphs.zh: “如果有人分享我所爱之人，即便我的灵魂因此消逝，我也要杀死我所爱之人，喊道：‘哦灵魂，宁可英勇赴死，也不愿与他人共享这份情愫。’”

paragraphs.en: He ordered his slave to strike me with the sword. As the slave prepared, he asked, "O my lady, do you have any final wish?" I replied, "Let him go so I can speak."
paragraphs.zh: 他命令仆人用剑打我。仆人准备动手时，主人问道：“夫人，您还有最后的心愿吗？”我说：“让他去，我要说话。”

paragraphs.en: Raising my head, I wept bitterly, reflecting on how I had fallen from grace and faced death.
paragraphs.zh: 抬起头来，我痛哭流涕，反思自己是如何失宠并面临死亡的威胁。

paragraphs.en: My husband looked at me angrily and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 我的丈夫怒气冲冲地盯着我，然后说道：

paragraphs.en: Tell her who for another lover left, Bored with me, and repaid me with disdain, That even though I suffered first, I found Contentment in what was between us twain.
paragraphs.zh: 告诉她，那个移情别恋的女人厌倦了我，用轻蔑回报了我。尽管我是先受苦的，但在我们两人之间，我还是找到了满足。

paragraphs.en: Hearing his words, I wept and replied:
paragraphs.zh: 听到他的话，我泪眼婆娑地回答道：

paragraphs.en: You set my poor heart burning with your love And left my eyes to smart while you went to sleep, While all alone I thought of you and wept And in my sorrow did a vigil keep. You promised to be faithful to the end, But when you had my heart, you broke the vow. I loved you in all childish innocence; Kill not that love, for I am learning now.
paragraphs.zh: 你让我这颗可怜的心燃烧在爱中， 而你却让我双眼疼痛自己去忍受， 独自思念你，黯然神伤， 整夜守护着这份哀愁。 你曾承诺至死不渝， 但当你拥有我的心时，却违背了誓言。 我对你纯真地倾心， 不要摧毁这份爱， 因为我现在正在学会珍惜。

paragraphs.en: Angered by my response, he glared at me and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他见我,"); 愤然瞪了我一眼，然后冷声说道：

paragraphs.en: ’Twas not boredom that bid me leave my love, But a sin that imposed such fate on me. She wished to let another share our love, But faith forbade me such a blasphemy.
paragraphs.zh: 并不是无聊让我离开我的爱人，而是罪孽将这样的命运强加于我。她希望让另一个人分享我们的爱情，但信仰禁止我犯下如此亵渎神明的罪行。

paragraphs.en: I wept again and implored him, saying:
paragraphs.zh: 我又哭了，恳求他说：

paragraphs.en: You left me burdened with the weight of love, Being too weak even a shirt to wear. I marvel not that my soul wastes away But that my body can your absence bear.
paragraphs.zh: 你让我背负着爱的重担，连一件衬衫都穿不上。我惊讶于我的灵魂为何枯萎，更惊讶于我的身体还能忍受你的缺席。

paragraphs.en: He cursed and scolded me. Looking at me, he recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他咒骂着我，瞪着眼睛念道：

paragraphs.en: You left me to enjoy another love And showed disdain, a deed I could not do. If you dislike my presence, I will leave And rue the end of love, as you did rue, And take another lover for myself, For love was killed not by me but by you.
paragraphs.zh: 你撇下我另寻爱恋 展现了不屑之情 这是我做不到的 如果你不喜我的相伴 我将离开 反悔这段爱情的终结 如你当初般后悔 并另觅新欢 因为爱情并非因为我而消逝 而是你亲手葬送

paragraphs.en: He ordered a slave to cut the second lady in half, deeming her life worthless. Just as I resigned myself to death, an old woman rushed in, pleading with my husband: "Pardon her for my sake. You are still young; do not bear the guilt."
paragraphs.zh: 他命令一个奴隶将第二位夫人一分为二，认为她的生命毫无价值。就在我不情愿地接受死亡的时候，一位老妇人冲了进来，向我的丈夫恳求道：“为了我，请饶恕她吧。你还年轻，不要背上这份罪责。”

paragraphs.en: Her tears and pleas moved him, but he insisted on branding her instead. The slaves stripped me naked and stretched me on the floor. He beat me with a quince rod until I lost consciousness.
paragraphs.zh: 她的泪水和哀求打动了他，但他坚持要给她烙印。奴隶们把我剥得赤裸裸的，将我按在地板上。他用榅桲木棒抽打我，直到我不省人事。

paragraphs.en: They then took me home in darkness.
paragraphs.zh: 他们随后在黑暗中把我送回了家。

paragraphs.en: When I regained consciousness, my body was disfigured from the beating, and marks marred my sides. For four months, I lay sick in bed. Recovering, I sought out my husband's house but found it destroyed.
paragraphs.zh: 当我恢复知觉时，身体因鞭打而面目全非，两侧留下了伤痕。整整四个月，我卧病在床。康复后，我前往丈夫的住所，却发现那里已被毁弃。

paragraphs.en: The alley was torn down, leaving only piles of rubbish where his house once stood. Seeking solace, I visited my father’s sister, who greeted me with these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 小巷已被拆毁，昔日他家所在之处只剩下一片废墟。我前去投奔姑母，她迎接我说起了这些诗句：

paragraphs.en: "Such is the world; with patience it is best, The loss of wealth or love to breast."
paragraphs.zh: “这就是这个世界；以耐心应对，无论是财富还是爱情的丧失。”

paragraphs.en: She then shared her own tale, recounting how her sisters had wronged her and their current fates.
paragraphs.zh: 她随后讲述了自己遭遇的故事，叙述了姐妹们如何冤枉了她以及她们如今的境况。

paragraphs.en: We lived together without thinking of any man. Every day, the shopper would come to buy our daily needs from the market. This continued for a long time until one night when our sister returned with a porter who stayed to entertain us.
paragraphs.zh: 我们两人同居一室，心中全无其他男人的念头。每天，那位采购员都会前来为我们购买日常所需，从市场上带回各种物品。这种情况持续了很长时间，直到有一天晚上，我们的妹妹带着一名搬运工归来，那人留下来陪我们聊天解闷。

paragraphs.en: Shortly after midnight, three dervishes joined us and we conversed. Around dawn, three merchants from Mosul arrived, sharing their adventures before breaking a condition we had set. We pardoned them, and they left.
paragraphs.zh: 接近午夜时分，三位苦行僧加入我们的谈话。黎明前，又有三位来自摩苏尔的商贾抵达，他们分享了自己的奇遇，随后打破了我们设定的一个条件。我们宽恕了他们，他们便离开了。

paragraphs.en: The caliph was amazed by their tales. But morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad then said, "Sister, what an incredible story!"
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发被她们的故事惊呆了。但天亮了，沙赫拉兹沉默了下来。迪纳兹 then said, “妹妹，这真是个令人惊叹的故事！”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more to tell if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 沙弗拉扎德回答说：“等到了明天晚上再说吧，如果国王饶恕我，我还有很多故事要讲呢。”

paragraphs.en: That night, Shahrazad began again.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，沙海拉扎德又开始了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: The caliph, amazed by the tale, asked the first girl about the demon serpent that had bewitched her sisters. She replied, "O Commander of the Faithful, she gave me a tuft of hair, saying 'Burn two hairs when you need me, and I will come at once.'"
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发听了这个故事，不禁惊讶地问道：“贤良的领袖啊，她给了你一根头发，说‘当你需要我的时候，烧两根头发，我会立刻出现’？”

paragraphs.en: He requested to see the tuft of hair. After burning it, the palace trembled as the serpent appeared. The serpent greeted the caliph and expressed gratitude for saving her life.
paragraphs.zh: 他请求查看那撮头发。烧掉后，宫殿震动，蛇出现了。蛇向哈里发问好，并感激涕零地表示是您救了她的命。

paragraphs.en: She explained that she had turned her sisters into bitches out of revenge but was willing to release them if ordered.
paragraphs.zh: 她解释说，为了报复，她已经把姐妹们变成了所谓的“贱人”，但如果受到命令，她愿意释放她们。

paragraphs.en: The caliph declared, "O spirit, free them from their suffering." He promised to investigate the case of the flogged girl afterward, seeking justice for her. The serpent then revealed that the abuser was the caliph's closest companion and sprinkled water over the sisters to restore them to human form.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发宣布：“精灵啊，释放她们免受痛苦。”他承诺事后再调查那个鞭打女子的案件，为她讨回公道。随后，那条蛇透露出施暴者竟是哈里发最亲近的同伴，并向姐妹们洒下水，使她们恢复了人形。

paragraphs.en: The she-demon spoke: "O Commander of the Faithful, the man who flogged this girl is your son al-Amin, brother of al-Ma’mun. He tricked her into a legal marriage after hearing of her beauty and charm. Though he was about to kill her, he spared her by flogging her instead and sending her home.
paragraphs.zh: 女妖说道：“万民之主啊，鞭打此女的人是你儿子阿敏，阿里穆恩的兄弟。他听说她的美貌与魅力后，设下计谋将她骗入合法婚姻。虽然他本打算杀死她，但最终还是选择了鞭打她并放她回家。”

paragraphs.en: This is the story of the second girl."
paragraphs.zh: 这是第二个女子的故事。

paragraphs.en: When Harun heard this, he was greatly surprised. "Praise be to God," he said, "who has freed these women from sorcery and torture." He then summoned his son al-Amin for confirmation.
paragraphs.zh: 哈伦听到这话，大为惊讶。“谢天谢地，”他脱口而出，“感谢真主解救了这些女人免受巫术和折磨。”随后，他叫来儿子阿敏进行确认。

paragraphs.en: Harun assembled a group: the judge, witnesses, three dervishes (sons of kings), the first girl and her sisters under a spell, the flogged girl, and a shopper. After questioning, he married the first girl and her sisters to the dervishes, making them chamberlains with wealth and a palace in Baghdad.
paragraphs.zh: 哈伦召集了一群人：法官、证人、三位来自王室的苦行僧（即三个兄弟）、被施了咒语的第一位女子及其姐妹、受鞭笞的女孩以及一名商贩。经过一番询问后，他将第一位女子和她的姐妹们许配给了苦行僧，并让他们成为宫中的近侍，拥有财富和巴格达的一座宫殿。

paragraphs.en: Next, he married the flogged girl to al-Amin under a new contract, showering her with riches and ordering a better house for her. Finally, Harun himself married the third girl, the shopper.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，他为受鞭笞的女孩与阿敏重新订立婚约，并让她享受丰厚的财富，还特意为她建造了一座更好的宅第。最后，哈伦自己娶了第三个女孩，那位经常外出购物的女人。

paragraphs.en: The people marveled at his wisdom, tolerance, and generosity as all facts were revealed.
paragraphs.zh: 人们惊叹于他展现出的智慧、宽容和慷慨，因为所有事实都浮出水面。
